title: Malachai, the Cruel Messenger
subtitle: Curses & Corruption

lore.description:
She was a herald, and her office was to arrive with the thing that could not be softened: the death, the verdict, the year the crop would fail. She was not cruel. She was necessary, and she was good at it, and she did it for a very long time.

Necessity wears. She began — kindly, at first, and only sometimes — to put something beside the truth when she delivered it. Never a lie. She has never in her existence told one. Just a second sentence after the true one: *and there may yet be a way*. She watched what that did to people's faces, and she went on doing it, because the faces were better.

That is the whole of her method and it has not changed since. She tells you the truth about your situation — accurately, in detail, more honestly than anyone in your life has been willing to — and then she adds the softening, and the softening is yours to finish. She will not argue you into anything. She does not need to. You will do the rest of the work yourself and you will do it in her voice and you will believe it was your idea, and every time it fails you will come back, because she was right about everything else.

For this the gods put her in black iron under Zahk'Kozahn, and she is chained and not contained, and her voice has never stopped.
lore.followers: Her followers learn that power demands suffering, mastering gifts that devour from within. Among the peoples of Fate's Edge, Malachai is the patron of the desperate and the damned. In Zakov, she is the Salt-Fang, whose silver coin appears in the mouth of drowned sailors. In the Valewood, she is the Thorn-Giver, invoked by hunters who curse a rival's bow. In Linn, she is the Wave-Mother's Shadow, whose gifts turn the tide of battle — at a price. Wherever hope curdles into despair, Malachai whispers.
lore.quote: I offer you everything you desire, and everything you fear. The payment comes later.
lore.the_city:
There were people in Zahk'Kozahn before it was cursed. They are the ones who bound her, and they were right to, and they did it well.

Her revenge took no force at all. She gave them what they had asked for — each of them, precisely, the thing they had wanted and named — and she gave it in full and without deceit and without limit, and she has gone on giving it every day since. And beside each gift she set the other thing they had named, in the dark, the one they had been frightened of, and she keeps that supplied too.

They are still there. They have everything. Nobody who has walked through the lower city has been able to describe them afterward in a way that satisfies anyone, and the accounts do not agree except on one point, which is that they were not restrained and did not leave.

domain_focus: Cursed Gifts: Faustian bargains, power with hidden costs
Corruptive Power: tainted blessings, addictive magic
False Salvation: hope that destroys, beautiful lies
Supernatural Afflictions: vampirism, lycanthropy, and other curses

thiasos.description: A Runekeeper who serves Malachai does not bind a familiar of purity or light. Their Thiasos is a small creature touched by her corruption: a black rat with one red eye that gnaws at the bars of its cage, a crow with a broken feather that always points toward the nearest corpse, a toad that secretes a toxin causing fever dreams, a small bat that drinks blood from a silver dish, or a moth whose wing dust leaves a rash that itches for a week.
thiasos.care: This creature requires no food, but it must be given a small sacrifice of pain (a pinprick, a pinch of salt in a wound) each day. If neglected for a week, it becomes Compromised (it grows sullen and its aura of despair thickens, imposing –1 die on all Resolve rolls for its bearer until a proper curse is laid).

codex.description: No Codex of Malachai takes the form of a book of hope. It may be a chain of iron links, each etched with a curse; a box of cracked bells that toll when a Rite is spoken; a scroll of skin from a sinner who died unshriven; or a set of silver nails driven into a board, each nail a promise broken.
codex.upkeep: Because Malachai's truths are written in pain, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week pricking their finger and letting a drop of blood fall onto each nail (or each bell), or the curses stored there become faint (treat as Compromised until re-blooded).

patrons_gift.name: Malachai's Honeyed Word
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Malachai may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or garment) and whisper a false promise.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Intimidation or Deception rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would suffer a supernatural curse, they may ignore it (the curse slides off, seeking another target).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Malachai.

rites.name: Rite of the Honeyed Binding
rites.materials: Blood mixed with sweet wine, or a broken chain link.
rites.effect: Choose one: Honeyed Curse — target gains +2 dice to their next roll (counts as Triumph); they take 1 Corruption (unresistable). Binding Curse — target gains +1 die to physical actions but suffers Fatigue 1 unless they perform a dominance act (beat a weaker creature, drink blood, break something precious).
rites.push_it: (Honeyed) Grant +3 dice and auto-Triumph; inflict 2 Corruption instead. (Binding) Grant +2 dice but Fatigue 2; mark 1 SB (Spades) as the curse's hunger grows. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the False Dawn
rites.materials: Meteoric iron shard blessed by false light.
rites.effect: Bestow a gift with a hidden curse. Target gains a significant advantage (e.g., +1 die to all rolls for one scene) but accrues a 4-segment Corruption timer. Each time they use the gift, tick the timer. When full, they suffer a related curse (GM chooses: festering wounds, beastly urges, or the attention of a Collector).
rites.push_it: The gift is more powerful (+2 dice, or extended duration). The timer advances 2 segments immediately; mark 1 SB (Diamonds). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Cruel Transformation
rites.materials: Holy water mixed with graveyard dust.
rites.effect: Infect a target with a supernatural condition (vampiric hunger, bestial rage, shadow-bind). Lasts one scene. Start a 6-segment Transformation timer. Each time the target resists feeding or transformation, tick the timer. When full, the condition becomes permanent.
rites.push_it: The condition becomes permanent immediately; target gains +1 die to relevant actions but is marked by Malachai (a Collector will visit within a week). Mark 1 SB (Hearts). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Messenger's Burden
rites.materials: Manacles worn while speaking her name.
rites.effect: Channel Malachai directly. Gain +2 dice to one action per beat this scene, but each use marks 1 SB as her influence spreads. Start an 8-segment Corruption's Grip timer. When it fills, a Collector arrives to demand a memory, a name, or a year of your life.
rites.push_it: +3 dice but mark 2 SB, suffer Fatigue 1, and her voice becomes permanent — you hear whispers of cruel bargains in quiet moments. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Chained Angel's Tribute
rites.materials: A chapel bell cracked by divine lightning, or a silver coin that cannot be spent.
rites.effect: Corrupt a sacred space or consecrate a site to Malachai. Within the zone: supernatural effects gain +1 Effect; blessings and healing spells generate +1 SB on a failure; any creature that accepts a gift from Malachai within the zone immediately ticks a Corruption timer twice. Start a 10-segment Divine Perversion timer. When it fills, the site becomes a permanent beacon for the Worn — the ghouls of Zahk'Kozahn.
rites.push_it: The corruption spreads to adjacent areas; mark 3 SB (Diamonds). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Malachai sings in harmonies of sweet despair — melodies that begin like a lullaby and end like a scream. Their voice is used to lure the desperate into bargains, to make a village accept a curse as a blessing, or to sing a monster to sleep so that it may be bound. Malachai's Cantors are terrifying not because they are evil, but because they are willing to do evil — they will poison the well to teach the town to dig deeper, or curse a child to save a hundred adults. They are hated and needed in equal measure.

cult.name: The Cult of the Leashed Hunger
cult.description: Malachai's cults gather in places where suffering is already present: plague hospitals, slums, refugee camps, and the cells of the condemned. The most fanatical cell, the Leashed Hunger, meets in catacombs beneath Zahk'Kozahn's ruins, where they drink water from the Well of Ichor and carve the names of their victims into their own flesh with silver needles. A ritual involves each member naming a curse they have inflicted (or allowed) and a mercy they have buried because of it. Then they prick their finger and let a drop of blood fall into a cracked bell; the bell tolls once, and a Collector appears to witness. Their creed is whispered, not spoken: 'We are the knife that cuts the rot. The wound heals, but the scar remembers us.' Outsiders are not welcome; they are patients, or potential tools, or future victims. Those who die serving Malachai become the Worn — shambling ghouls that guard the cursed city.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Curse-Smith
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Malachai is a curse-smith or affliction-weaver — one who crafts pain into purpose. Their magic works through the materials of suffering: a needle that sews a nightmare into a pillow, a forge that tempers a blade to always strike the wielder's loved ones, or a garden where belladonna and hemlock grow in geometric patterns. In Aeler, a True-Mason might carve a keystone that makes every tenth step collapse, but a witch of Malachai would instead sew a curse-seam into the mortar, so that the tunnel itself remembers every injury it has caused.
witchcraft.lore: The curse-smith's path is precision, not cruelty for its own sake. They learn that a curse well-aimed is a scalpel, not a cudgel — that the worst afflictions are small, specific, and patient. Malachai's witches are called on by desperate people for desperate reasons: a landlord who deserves ruin, a soldier who cannot stop killing, a debt that must be paid by someone. They rarely ask whether the reasons are good enough.
witchcraft.quote: The wound heals. The scar remembers us.

splintered_needle.name: The Splintered Needle
splintered_needle.description: A needle of black iron, snapped in half and re-joined with a drop of the witch's blood. Once per session, the witch may sew a 'curse seam' into a garment, a threshold, or a skin. The curse is small but specific: a button that falls off at the worst moment, a door that sticks when someone is pursued, a hand that trembles when holding a weapon. The target suffers –1 die on a single type of roll for the scene. The witch may unstitch the curse as a free action, but doing so marks 1 Fatigue.

hedge_gifts.name: Borrowed Scars
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may touch a fresh wound (inflicted within the last hour) and speak a single word of Malachai's name. For the remainder of the scene, the witch may transfer the pain of that wound (as 1 Fatigue) to another creature within Near range. The target resists with Spirit+Endurance (DV 3); on a failure, they suffer the Fatigue and the witch's original wound heals slightly (clear 1 Fatigue from themselves). On a success, the witch takes the Fatigue anyway — the curse rebounds.

hedge_gifts.name: Small Malediction
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, name a minor, specific inconvenience to befall a target you can see within Near (a stumble, a dropped item, a coughing fit). It happens at the next dramatically appropriate moment, at the GM's discretion, imposing –1 die on their next roll.

hedge_gifts.name: Well of Ichor Draught
hedge_gifts.description: You may brew a bitter tonic during downtime that, when drunk, grants +1 die to resist fear or despair for the rest of the day — at the cost of one vivid, unpleasant dream that night. Requires a private working space and a personal sacrifice of pain.

monastic_tradition.name: The Order of the Unshriven
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Unshriven Order train in places others abandon — plague wards, execution grounds, the cells beneath courthouses. They believe that suffering, faced honestly and without flinching, is the only true purification, and that Malachai's curses are simply the world's ledger made visible. Their discipline is grim and exact: they learn to carry pain without breaking, to inflict it without cruelty, and to recognize when a curse has become a mercy in disguise.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Spirit 3+, Resolve 2+, Rite of the Honeyed Binding or Cantor of Malachai.
monastic_tradition.quote: We are the knife that cuts the rot.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Unshriven have already paid their worst debts in advance, in pain freely offered. Monks gain +1 die to resist any curse, geas, or Obligation that would be inflicted upon them involuntarily. If they succeed, the curse instead marks a small, visible toll on the one who tried to inflict it — a bruise, a cough, a moment of their own despair made plain.

basic.name: Scar Ledger
basic.description: Once per scene, mark 1 Fatigue to gain +2 dice on a single roll to endure, resist, or push through pain, fear, or a supernatural affliction.

advanced.name: Reader of Debts
advanced.description: Once per scene, look upon a person or place and sense the shape of the curse or affliction that clings to them (GM answers one question about its nature, source, or trigger).

master.name: The Mercy Cut
master.description: Once per session, take a target's active curse or supernatural affliction onto yourself for the remainder of the scene, sparing them its effects entirely. You suffer the affliction's mechanical effects for that time; afterward, the affliction returns to its original bearer unless you have found another way to end it.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Sharpened Senses: +1 die to Notice in dim light.
corruption.cost: Unsettling Presence: –1 die to social warmth checks.

corruption.benefit: Primal Vigor: +1 die to Athletics and physical actions.
corruption.cost: Dark Hunger: 1 Fatigue if a day passes without feeding (blood or rare herbs).

corruption.benefit: Unnatural Resilience: Once per session, resist one Condition.
corruption.cost: Beastly Tells: Failures cause visible physical changes (slitted eyes, fur patches).

corruption.benefit: Cursed Vigour: Natural weapons count as magical; +1 Effect.
corruption.cost: Transformed Body: Permanent physical change (eye color, skin texture, etc.).

corruption.benefit: Regenerative Curse: Heal 1 Fatigue or Condition per rest.
corruption.cost: Corruption's Price: Pushing rites adds permanent Corruption (cannot be cleared).

corruption.benefit: Monstrous Ascendant: +2 dice to Body-based actions; your unarmed strikes deal +1 Harm and count as magical.
corruption.cost: Loss of Self: The GM may compel curse-driven behavior (feed, rage, corrupt) once per session. You can resist with Spirit+Endurance (DV 4). On failure, you act according to the curse for one exchange. Your eyes now glow faintly red in darkness — a visible sign of Malachai's claim.

playstyle_notes.description:
Malachai is the setting's study of addiction and should be run as one. The gift is real, it works, and it is genuinely the best available option at the moment it is taken — that is not a trick, and a GM who plays it as a trick has lost the thread. The harm is that it works.

Her voice is never a temptation scene. It is an accurate account of the character's situation, delivered with more honesty and more attention than anyone else in the fiction has offered them, followed by one soft sentence the player completes on their own. Let the player do the rationalizing; never write it for them. And let her be right, repeatedly, about everything except the one thing.

**Content note:** addiction, loss of self, and the consequences of desperate choices. Use Lines & Veils, and check in — this patron works by making the player complicit in the reasoning, which is precisely why it lands and precisely why it needs consent.
emphasizes: Cursed Gifts: power that always costs more than expected
Addiction as Magic: once you start, stopping is harder than any curse
False Salvation: every cure is a waiting room
Supernatural Afflictions: becoming the monster to fight monsters
The Chained Angel: patient, hungry, and never truly contained

sample_adventure.title: The Well of Ichor
sample_adventure.description: A plague has broken out in a refugee camp on the road to Zahk'Kozahn, and a Leashed Hunger cell has begun offering a cure — for a price paid in memory and flesh. The cure works. The party must decide whether to expose the cult, negotiate with it, or accept that in a camp with no other physician, Malachai's mercy may be the only mercy available. Whatever they choose, someone in the camp will not survive the choosing, and Malachai will remember who made it.
sample_adventure.quote: You wanted the fever to break. It has. Ask yourself what else broke with it.
